data.description:
## Description

What: New plugins/dso/scripts/pr-destructive-action.sh <pr-number> <action> [args...] that internally invokes pr-owned-by-session.sh, then on exit 0 executes 'gh pr <action> [args...]', and on exit 1/2/3 emits structured stderr with the case identifier and exits non-zero (fail-closed). Why: Per the bot-psychologist R2 lesson, enforcement must be structural — a single permitted path that internalizes the check, not a 'remember to check first' composition. Scope IN: the internal-check-then-act control flow; fail-closed behavior on all non-own cases; a shell unit test covering all 4 internal-check outcomes end-to-end; the two-session integration test (session A stamps + acts succeeds; session B refused exit 1 on close/merge/comment; stripped-trailer exit 2). Scope OUT: the PreToolUse hook (draft-5); call-site migration (draft-7).


## Done Definitions

- pr-destructive-action.sh internally invokes pr-owned-by-session.sh and executes 'gh pr <action> [args...]' only when that check exits 0; on exit 1/2/3 it emits structured stderr with the case identifier and exits non-zero (fail-closed) ← Satisfies: sc-3
- A shell unit test covers all four internal-check outcomes (own/foreign/absent/api_error) end-to-end through the wrapper ← Satisfies: sc-3
- A two-session integration test: session A (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=session-A-uuid) creates a trailer-stamped synthetic PR and successfully acts on it; session B (session-B-uuid) is refused (exit 1, structured stderr) on close, merge, and comment; a PR with a stripped trailer returns exit 2 (absent) ← Validates Closure Check: "Two-session integration test: simulate session A with CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=session-A-uuid creating a synthetic PR (trailer stamped); switch to CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=session-B-uuid and attempt close/merge/comment via pr-destructive-action.sh — all three refused (exit 1, structured stderr). Positive case (session A acts on its own PR) succeeds. Edge case (PR with stripped trailer) returns exit 2 absent — included in the same test."

## Considerations

- [Structural] R2 lesson: the wrapper must INTERNALIZE the check (single permitted path), never delegate the check-then-act ordering to a caller's discipline.
- [Concurrency] Same-session concurrent destructive actions are intended-permitted (0777-0f3d); an advisory lock is explicitly deferred per the epic HIGH scenario.
- [Isolation] The two-session integration test must run in a configuration-isolated environment (empty HOME, no pre-set CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID inherited from the developer machine) so CI-runner behavior is validated, not the developer's ambient session.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a DSO session, I want pr-destructive-action.sh as the single permitted path for destructive PR actions that internalizes the ownership check and fails closed, so that no destructive gh pr action can run on a PR this session does not own.
